counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span documents an external incentive, so malingering is not fully excluded
Repeated lorazepam challenge tests had limited effect and appeared to reinforce the behaviors
Benign neurologic examination and absence of tongue biting argue against true seizures
decisive_items: Clues suggesting volitional behavior included selective acceptance of benzodiazepines and gabapentin while refusing other medications

eating all meals despite “stupor,” abruptly lapsing into and out of catatonia-like and psychotic behaviors depending on the topic of conversation, purposeful movements to obtain lorazepam after seizures, and evidence of self‐induced urinary incontinence during one episode.
response.rationale: C1 is strongest because its raw spans cover the full volitional-behavior clue sequence, including eating all meals despite stupor, and its label specifies factitious disorder imposed on self. R4 is a close broader correlate but lacks the eating-all-meals span and subtype specificity. R2 relies only on the historical borderline personality disorder label and does not address the volitional symptom-producing behaviors.

rejected.why: Its only raw support is the historical diagnosis 'borderline personality disorder'; it ignores the volitional behavior clues and the catatonia specialist's assessment, making it a less likely primary diagnosis.
